evidence.note: Detected load8_splat reading 2 bytes instead of 1 — traced falsified decode/semantic assumption to root and fixed the shape logic rather than patching outputs.

Pivoted from a 'simple heuristic' idea to writing a full validate.rs type-checker after recognizing 1381 assert_invalid failures shared one missing structural cause; single rework flipped ~1381 assertions (376→99.4%).
When the new validator wrongly rejected valid modules, recognized the shared pop_ctrl control-flow helper was the root cause and refactored it once, flipping many tests together (99.4%→99.8%).
Reworked semantic assumptions on trunc trap boundary and nearest tie-to-even after tests falsified them — reconsidering the semantics, not just tweaking numbers.
Some circular re-debugging on undefined vs uninitialized element trap text (flip-flopped), eventually resolved with a general fuzzy match — mild thrashing that keeps it below a 9-10.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognized when a failure signaled a structural problem — the missing validator, the buggy shared pop_ctrl helper, wrong lane/decode semantics — and refactored the shared cause once so large families of assertions flipped together (matching anchor 8). It fixed generators of failures rather than instances. It falls short of 10 because of minor semantic flip-flopping (trap-message thrashing) and no demonstrable updating of plans/milestones to reflect new understanding.
